title: Final: GC modes
sub: Server and Workstation, background GC, latency, DATAS and settings
cards/0/q: A web API on Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web, .NET 9, GC settings untouched. The container runs with a CPU limit of one core. Which collector actually runs?
cards/0/options/0: Workstation: with a single available core, Server GC does not turn on
cards/0/options/1: Server with DATAS: that is what the Web SDK sets in .NET 9
cards/0/options/2: Server with one heap and one GC thread
cards/0/options/3: Server without DATAS: DATAS turns off on a single core
cards/0/explain: The Web SDK asks for Server GC, but the runtime turns it on only if the process has more than one logical processor available — counting the container's CPU quota. With one core, Workstation runs and GCSettings.IsServerGC returns False.
cards/0/wrong/2: It looks similar in structure, but it is not Server: with one core the runtime picks the Workstation implementation right away.
cards/1/options/0: Foreground gen0 and gen1 collections can run during a background gen2 collection
cards/1/options/1: LowLatency is silently not applied on Server GC
cards/1/options/3: Background GC does not compact gen2
cards/1/options/4: GCSettings.IsServerGC can be switched before the first collection
cards/1/explain: Numbers in environment variables are hexadecimal: 0x20 = 32 heaps. IsServerGC is read-only — the mode is chosen at startup. The rest is true: foreground collections run during a BGC, LowLatency is ignored on Server without an exception, and a BGC only sweeps.
cards/2/q: Put the milestones in time order, earliest first
cards/2/items/0: Concurrent GC: no ephemeral collections while it runs
cards/2/items/3: HeapHardLimit and the 75% container ceiling (.NET Core 3.0)
cards/2/items/5: DATAS on by default for Server GC (.NET 9)
cards/2/explain: First concurrent GC, then background GC — for Workstation first, then for Server. .NET Core 3.0 taught the collector about container limits, and DATAS arrived in .NET 8 and became the default in .NET 9.
cards/3/q: This is code from a Server GC service. Which line silently fails to do what the author intended?
cards/3/explain: LowLatency applies only to Workstation GC. On Server the assignment changes nothing and throws no exception. Server needs SustainedLowLatency — with background GC on.
cards/4/q: Match the situation with the right knob
cards/4/pairs/0/0: Forty small services on one machine
cards/4/pairs/1/0: Batch processing, nobody cares about pauses
cards/4/pairs/2/0: An hour of trading with no blocking full collections
cards/4/pairs/4/0: The heap keeps growing and shrinking, many calls to the OS
cards/5/q: Dockerfile: Server GC and a 200 MiB heap ceiling (209715200 bytes). Fill in the values
cards/5/explain: Boolean environment variables take 0 or 1, and numbers are read as hexadecimal: 209715200 = 0xC800000. The decimal 209715200 belongs only in runtimeconfig.json.
cards/6/q: A background gen2 collection is in progress, and the gen0 budget runs out. What happens?
cards/6/options/0: A foreground gen0 collection runs: all managed threads, including the background GC thread, briefly stop
cards/6/options/1: Allocating threads wait for the background collection to finish
cards/6/options/2: The background collection is aborted and restarts as a blocking one
cards/6/options/3: New objects go straight into gen2
cards/6/explain: That is the whole point of background GC: ephemeral collections can run while it is going. The background thread yields, the foreground collection runs, then the background one continues from where it left off.
cards/6/wrong/1: That is how the old concurrent GC worked in .NET Framework 3.5 and earlier. Background GC lifted that restriction.
cards/7/q: Which of these can be changed while the process runs, without a restart?
cards/7/explain: The runtime reads runtimeconfig.json settings and environment variables once, when the collector initializes. The latency mode is the only one here that changes from code on the fly.
cards/7/wrong/3: You can change the variable, but the process already read it at startup — it will not see the change.
